title: Package manifest
description: Packages installed by `platform/bootstrap.nu`. Each package is installed with the first manager in priority order that has an entry for it.

platforms.description: Settings shared by all systems of a platform. Names match `$nu.os-info.name`.

systems.description: Supported systems. Linux systems are detected from `ID` / `ID_LIKE` in `/etc/os-release`.

managers.description: Package managers and how to drive them. Commands run in the shell of the platform they are used on.

packages.description: Packages to install, keyed by a system independent name. Packages without entries for any manager of the current platform are skipped silently.

platformName.description: Name of a platform defined under `platforms`. Keep in sync with the manifest, `bootstrap.nu` reports mismatches.

systemName.description: Name of a system defined under `systems`. Keep in sync with the manifest, `bootstrap.nu` reports mismatches.

managerName.description: Name of a manager defined under `managers`. Keep in sync with the manifest, `bootstrap.nu` reports mismatches.

command.description: Command executed with the platform `shell`: POSIX `sh` on linux and macos, `powershell` on windows.

shell.description: Program and arguments every command is passed to as the last argument, e.g. `[sh, -c]`.

prepare.description: Command run once before installing anything, the run aborts when it fails.

path.description: Directories prepended to `PATH` so freshly installed tools are found, `~` is expanded.

platform.description: Platform whose settings apply to this system.

match.description: Values of `ID` / `ID_LIKE` from `/etc/os-release` that select this system. Required when several systems share a platform.

managers.description: Managers available on this system in default priority order. Managers are processed in this order, so a manager may only require packages provided by managers listed before it.

install.description: Install command. `{pkgs}` installs a batch of packages at once, `{pkg}` runs the command once per package. Managers without it only run the commands given by package entries.

requires.description: Package keys that must be installed before this manager is used.

check.description: When this command succeeds `setup` is skipped. When it fails and there is no `setup`, the manager is unavailable.

setup.description: Command run once before the first install with this manager.

refresh.description: Command run after any of the manager's repos were enabled.

repos.description: Named repositories, enabled only when a selected package references them.

check.description: When this command succeeds the repository is considered enabled.

entry.description: How the package is installed with this manager: `true` uses the package key as the name, a string is the package name, a mapping allows extra options.

name.description: Package name for this manager, defaults to the package key.

repo.description: Repository (or list of repositories) from `managers.<manager>.repos` to enable first.

check.description: When this command succeeds the package is considered installed.

run.description: Command used instead of the manager's `install`.

check.description: When this command succeeds the package is considered installed.

prefer.description: Managers to try first, overriding the system order. A manager or list applies to every system, a mapping sets it per system.

package.description: Package sources per manager. Packages without a source on the current system are reported and skipped.

platforms.description: Platforms the package is restricted to, e.g. a linux desktop tool installed with a cross-platform manager like `cargo`.
